lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Experience should appear above Education.
items.because: Five years of full-time work should carry the page rather than the MBA.

items.says: The Experience section is not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Crestline appears above the more recent Harbor Payments internship, making the timeline harder to follow.

items.says: Coastal Marine Services needs to be shortened or its relevance explained.
items.because: The diesel-mechanic role reads as unrelated to the product, operations and consulting narrative.

items.says: The dry-dock wording attributes the entire turnaround result to rebuilding engines and gearboxes.
items.because: Other repairs, parts availability and dock logistics also determine total dry-dock time.

items.says: “Owned” and the meeting description bury the actual action.
items.because: The wording states an assigned responsibility but not what you did in the review.

items.says: The forecast-error result comes after the cadence, scope and method.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the strongest evidence in the bullet.

items.says: “Quarterly” and “12 consecutive quarters” repeat the cadence.
items.because: One phrase adds little evidence and takes space from the result or scope.

items.says: The driver-hour result comes after a long chain of implementation details.
items.because: The clearest proof of value is harder to find.

items.says: “Cutting” attributes the reduction in time to first payment to the redesign without a comparison method.
items.because: The figures show an observed reduction, but not necessarily that the verification step caused it.

items.says: The line treats support-ticket counts as RICE Reach without defining them as a proxy.
items.because: Reach estimates distinct users or customers, while raw tickets can include repeat contacts.

items.says: The RICE prioritization has no stated consequence.
items.because: The reader sees the decision process but not what changed or what value followed.

items.says: “RICE” is unexplained jargon.
items.because: Readers outside product management may not know what the framework represents.

items.says: The long method list comes before the roadmap decision.
items.because: The result is easy to miss and the analysis reads like a task list.

items.says: The session-randomized result is reported as an effect on merchants’ customers.
items.because: Session randomization directly estimates session-level conversion, not automatically a customer-level effect.

items.says: The five-point lift lacks a defined conversion measure and comparison.
items.because: The reader cannot tell the unit or which conversion event was measured.

items.says: The checkout A/B test and its five-point lift are repeated in another bullet.
items.because: The duplicate consumes space without adding evidence.

items.says: “To 3,100 students” does not say what was measured.
items.because: The students could have been reached, registered or using the app.

items.says: The launch bullet gives no specific product-lead contribution beyond launching the app.
items.because: The reader cannot see the product or execution skill behind the outcome.

items.says: “That would have been thrown away” buries the food-rescue outcome.
items.because: The relative clause slows the scan of the 9-tonne result.

items.says: Calling the rise from 400 to 1,150 a 150% increase is arithmetically wrong.
items.because: An increase of 750 from 400 is 187.5%.

items.says: The rise from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase is approximately 26.7%.

items.says: “$2.4M annual saving” presents a modeled estimate as an actual saving.
items.because: Funding a pilot does not establish that the saving was realized.

items.says: “Sized a $2.4M annual saving” is awkward phrasing.
items.because: Savings are usually estimated or quantified rather than sized.

items.says: The front-desk adoption result comes after passive process details.
items.because: The candidate’s action and the practical outcome are harder to distinguish.

items.says: The pilot approval comes after the presentation wording.
items.because: The clearest evidence of client impact is harder to scan.

items.says: “The final recommendation” does not identify what was recommended.
items.because: The reader cannot connect the presentation to the scheduling solution.

items.says: The scheduling-pilot approval is repeated in another bullet.
items.because: Repeating the same outcome uses space without showing an additional result.
